technology.wrong: To the extent that algorithms decide, human agency is diminished.
technology.correct: To the extent that algorithms decide, human agency is diminished. (correct!)

technology.wrong: Not that I disagree with the premise, but the execution was flawed.
technology.correct: Not that I disagree with the premise, but the execution was flawed. (correct!)
technology.error: not that = it's not that, correct usage

technology.wrong: The fewer the regulations, the more innovation there is.
technology.correct: The fewer the regulations, the more innovation there is. (correct!)

education.wrong: That the system is broken is beyond dispute; what to do about it less clear.
education.correct: That the system is broken is beyond dispute; what to do about it is less clear.

education.wrong: As pedagogical methods go, this one is decidedly antiquated.
education.correct: As pedagogical methods go, this one is decidedly antiquated. (correct!)
education.error: 'as X go' is a correct idiomatic structure

education.wrong: Equally as important as academic skills are social skills.
education.correct: Equally important as academic skills are social skills.
education.error: redundant: equally OR as, not both

education.wrong: Not until we address inequality can we claim that education is fair.
education.correct: Not until we address inequality can we claim that education is fair. (correct!)

education.wrong: It's not the grades per say that matter, but the learning process.
education.correct: It's not the grades per se that matter, but the learning process.

education.wrong: All things being equal, a degree from a prestigious university would advantage one.
education.correct: All things being equal, a degree from a prestigious university would give one an advantage.
education.error: advantage is a noun, not a verb in this context

education.wrong: The rationale behind standardized testing, however well-intentioned, are flawed.
education.correct: The rationale behind standardized testing, however well-intentioned, is flawed.

education.wrong: To what extent education should be liberal is a matter of debate.
education.correct: To what extent education should be liberal is a matter of debate. (correct!)

culture.wrong: Perish the thought that globalization might homogenize all cultures.
culture.correct: Perish the thought that globalization might homogenize all cultures. (correct!)
culture.error: perish the thought = heaven forbid, correct usage

culture.wrong: Would that we could preserve every endangered language.
culture.correct: Would that we could preserve every endangered language. (correct!)
culture.error: would that... = if only..., correct subjunctive

culture.wrong: The cultural artifacts, regardless of where they currently reside, belongs to their country of origin.
culture.correct: The cultural artifacts, regardless of where they currently reside, belong to their country of origin.

culture.wrong: Such is the diversity of the city that one can hear dozens of languages daily.
culture.correct: Such is the diversity of the city that one can hear dozens of languages daily. (correct!)

culture.wrong: As it were, cultural exchange is a two-way street.
culture.correct: As it were, cultural exchange is a two-way street. (correct!)
culture.error: as it were = so to speak, correct usage

culture.wrong: By dint of immigration, the city's culinary scene transformed.
culture.correct: By dint of immigration, the city's culinary scene was transformed.
culture.error: passive or intransitive: needs 'was transformed' or 'has been transformed'

culture.wrong: Insofar as culture defines identity, losing one's culture is traumatic.
culture.correct: Insofar as culture defines identity, losing one's culture is traumatic. (correct!)
culture.error: correct usage of insofar as = to the extent that

culture.wrong: If ever there was a melting pot, this city is it.
culture.correct: If ever there was a melting pot, this city is it. (correct!)

nature.wrong: Gone are the days when we could ignore climate science.
nature.correct: Gone are the days when we could ignore climate science. (correct!)

nature.wrong: Be the solution technological or behavioral, action must be swift.
nature.correct: Be the solution technological or behavioral, action must be swift.
nature.error: though old-fashioned, this is grammatically correct — be = whether it be

nature.wrong: Were it not for the Amazon rainforest, global temperatures would skyrocketed.
nature.correct: Were it not for the Amazon rainforest, global temperatures would skyrocket.
nature.error: would + bare infinitive, not past participle

nature.wrong: So dire is the situation as inaction is no longer an option.
nature.correct: So dire is the situation that inaction is no longer an option.

nature.wrong: The biodiversity of the region, along with its unique ecosystems, are under threat.
nature.correct: The biodiversity of the region, along with its unique ecosystems, is under threat.

nature.wrong: Never before has humanity faced a challenge of this magnitude.
nature.correct: Never before has humanity faced a challenge of this magnitude. (correct!)

nature.wrong: To blame are not just corporations but also consumers.
nature.correct: To blame are not just corporations but also consumers. (correct!)

nature.wrong: Little did scientists realized the full extent of the damage.
nature.correct: Little did scientists realize the full extent of the damage.

arts.wrong: Far from being obsolete, the novel has evolved in the digital age.
arts.correct: Far from being obsolete, the novel has evolved in the digital age. (correct!)

arts.wrong: Be it theatre or cinema, live performance has a unique power.
arts.correct: Be it theatre or cinema, live performance has a unique power. (correct!)
arts.error: correct subjunctive: be it = whether it be

arts.wrong: That the painting is a forgery is neither here nor there; its beauty remains.
arts.correct: That the painting is a forgery is neither here nor there; its beauty remains. (correct!)
arts.error: correct: neither here nor there = irrelevant

arts.wrong: Not for nothing did Picasso once say that art is a lie that makes us realize truth.
arts.correct: Not for nothing did Picasso once say that art is a lie that makes us realize truth. (correct!)

arts.wrong: The less commercialized art becomes, the more authentic it is.
arts.correct: The less commercialized art becomes, the more authentic it is. (correct!)

arts.wrong: Were the gallery to exhibit my work, I would be thrill.
arts.correct: Were the gallery to exhibit my work, I would be thrilled.

arts.wrong: All the more reason to support emerging artists.
arts.correct: All the more reason to support emerging artists. (correct!)

arts.wrong: Masterpiece though it may be, the film lacks emotional depth.
arts.correct: Masterpiece though it may be, the film lacks emotional depth. (correct!)
arts.error: correct 'noun + though + subject + may be' structure

health.wrong: Far be it for me to dispense medical advice, but you should see a doctor.
health.correct: Far be it from me to dispense medical advice, but you should see a doctor.

health.wrong: So deleterious are the effects of stress that it can literally shorten one's lifespan.
health.correct: So deleterious are the effects of stress that they can literally shorten one's lifespan.

health.wrong: Be that as it may, one cannot ignore the correlation between diet and longevity.
health.correct: Be that as it may, one cannot ignore the correlation between diet and longevity. (correct!)

health.wrong: For all the advances in medicine, lifestyle diseases are on the rise.
health.correct: For all the advances in medicine, lifestyle diseases are on the rise. (correct!)
health.error: for all = despite all, correct usage

health.wrong: It is indeed a paradox that the wealthier a society becomes, the unhealthier its citizens are.
health.correct: It is indeed a paradox that the wealthier a society becomes, the less healthy its citizens are.

health.wrong: Nowhere is the link between poverty and poor health more stark.
health.correct: Nowhere is the link between poverty and poor health more stark. (correct!)

health.wrong: Would that governments invested more in preventative healthcare.
health.correct: Would that governments invested more in preventative healthcare. (correct!)
health.error: would that = if only, correct subjunctive

health.wrong: To the extent which social determinants affect health, policy must address them.
health.correct: To the extent that social determinants affect health, policy must address them.
